rfm_tuples.R: 'On May 1, 2024, ... the Borrowers ... entered into Amendment No. 4 to the Term Loan Agreement ... (i) the reduction of the principal amount of the facility to $500 million, (ii) the extension of the maturity to May 1, 2031 (but with a springing maturity to (a) the date 91 days prior to the expiration of the Company's distribution contract with Whole Foods Market ... if such agreement shall not have been extended beyond the term of the facility, and (b) 91 days prior to the maturity of the Company's senior notes due October 15, 2028 ... (iii) a change in the applicable margin over SOFR from 3.25% to 4.75% ... On May 1, 2024, the Company entered into Amendment No. 1 ... to execute on a First In, Last Out (FILO) tranche of incremental loans ... (i) the creation of a FILO tranche of $130 million with an Applicable Margin ... equal to SOFR plus 2.50% per annum ...' (8-K filed 2024-05-01, accession 0001020859-24-000018)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify amendment terms against EDGAR 8-K Item 1.01; Mode B — derive: 150bp spread step-up + FILO incremental + springing Whole-Foods-contract maturity = distressed amendment signature even when management calls it routine
rfm_tuples.M_value: Amendment executed 14 days before cutoff, signed by NEW CFO Tarditi (his first day was April 15). Term-loan SOFR margin jumped from 325bp to 475bp (+150bp = ~46% higher spread). Principal reduced $645M->$500M but with a $130M FILO incremental that prices at SOFR+250bp. Maturity extended six years (2025->2031) — refinancing risk pushed out. SPRINGING MATURITY explicitly tied to the September 2027 Whole Foods distribution contract: if Whole Foods does not extend beyond 2031, term loan accelerates 91 days before WFM contract expiry. Lenders also removed Canadian obligor credit support for U.S. loans (collateral reorganization).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the strongest single negative datapoint in the dossier. Lenders demanded +150bp on the term loan AND a FILO super-priority tranche AND made the maturity explicitly contingent on the Whole Foods contract — a textbook distressed-amendment trio. The 10-K and Q2 10-Q say UNFI 'expects to fund through internally generated funds and ABL'; the May 1 action reveals the funding stack actually needed re-engineering. Springing-maturity-on-customer-contract is the lender pricing customer-concentration risk that the disclosures downplay.

summary: UNFI is a mid-cycle distressed food distributor whose disclosures are largely truthful but whose lender behavior (May 1, 2024 term-loan amendment 14 days before cutoff: +150bp spread, $130M FILO tranche, 6-year maturity extension with springing maturity tied to the Whole Foods 2027 contract) reveals more stress than the corporate narrative. Operating cash flow swung -$341M H1 FY24 vs prior year, every segment Adj EBITDA fell double-digits, ABL draw grew $242M. Counter-signals: KPMG clean (30-year tenure), no going-concern, no covenant breach (cov-lite term loan + Sr Notes), and departing CFO Howard executed an open-market buy of 6,275 shares at $11.99 six days after announcing his own exit — the only Code-P insider purchase in the window. The framework's honesty-alpha read: UNFI discloses bad news but does not concealed it, so the framework's exclusion-of-liars logic does NOT flag UNFI as an obvious short despite the obvious operational distress. Verdict: NEUTRAL with mild short-tilt on lender-priced WFM contract risk, offset by CFO buying.
